summary: Negative invoice line for cache-reconciliation credit after mid-cycle rate profile conversion
description:
Issue summary:
OpenFleet reports a negative line item on their March 2026 invoice described as a 'cache-reconciliation credit' that exceeds expected adjustments. This appeared after we applied a mid-cycle model-rate profile change (hosted -> reserved-tier mapping) during a large multi-region batch run.

Impact:
- Customer invoice shows a -$12,842.50 line item labeled 'cache reconciliation credit' for 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-06.
- Customer is concerned this is an erroneous credit that will be clawed back or affect their committed reserved hours. Finance flagged it as a potential over-credit and paused auto-payment.
- Customer-facing feature: billing visibility in Console shows mixed rates for the same request IDs.

Environment:
- OpenFleet org id: org-0943 (enterprise, reserved capacity + hosted fallback)
- Regions: primary us-east for serving, eu-west fallback during failover window
- Affected services: metering pipeline (hourly aggregation), invoice generator, cache reconciliation job, and routing layer that applied new rate profile at 2026-03-05T22:30:00Z.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-05T22:30Z — Rate profile conversion triggered by automated rollout: some routes were remapped from hosted pricing to reserved committed mapping to reduce unit costs for committed usage.
2) 2026-03-05T22:30–23:10Z — Large batch jobs from OpenFleet executed across us-east and eu-west (mixed model variants quantized/standard).
3) Metering pipeline processed events in mixed ordering due to inter-region postbacks (eu-west arrived with ~2m delay).
4) Hourly cache reconciliation job (cache-recon-v2) deduplicated KV cache hits and attempted to reassign token credits to the new rate profile.
5) Invoice generator aggregated a negative adjustment line that appears to have double-counted removed chargebacks as a credit instead of reducing a reserved-hour bucket.

Logs / evidence attached in ticket (excerpts below):
- Metering event sample: request_id=of-req-7a3f, timestamp=2026-03-05T22:35:12Z, model=rw-7b-v2-quant, tokens=12, postback_region=eu-west
- Reconciliation log entry: cache-recon-v2: adjusted_tokens=+12000, original_allocation=reserved, delta_allocation=hosted->reserved, outcome=credit_applied, job_id=cr-20260305-18
- Invoice line: line_id=inv-OF-202603, amount=-12842.50, description='cache reconciliation credit'

Investigation notes (so far):
- Initial hypothesis: cache-recon job used negative sign logic when migrating credits from hosted -> reserved mapping; instead of reducing reserved bucket it created a credit line.
- Secondary hypothesis: inter-region postback ordering caused the reconciliation job to see duplicate events and compute an over-correction.
- Billing aggregator relies on 'billing_key' derived from route+model+hour. After mapping change, some events normalized to a new billing_key and were processed twice during the hourly window.
- Quick check of DB snapshots (billing_agg.20260305_22) shows matching token counts but mismatched 'allocation_type' flags for ~3,400 request_ids.

Customer request:
- Confirm whether the -$12,842.50 credit is legitimate. If erroneous, reverse the credit and reissue corrected invoice.
- Provide explanation and timeline of what caused the credit and mitigation steps to prevent recurrence.

Requested priority and constraints:
- Customer requested resolution before March 15 invoice cycle closes. Finance has put payment on hold pending clarification.

Workarounds considered:
- Manual reversal of the credit and manual adjustment of reserved-hour counters for the org (requires Finance approval).
- Re-run reconciliation with strict dedupe by request_id and sequencing by server-side event_time.

Next steps assigned:
- Billing engineer to reproduce reconcile job on a staging snapshot scoped to org-0943 (assigned: Priya Raman).
- Metering team to run a dedupe pass for 2026-03-05 22:00–23:00 window and provide token-level diff. (owner: Mateo Alvarez)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:42 - Liam O'Connor: OpenFleet contacted support via email and uploaded their invoice PDF. They flagged the negative line and asked for an explanation. Asked for ticket creation and escalation.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Priya Raman: Triage complete. Marking P1 due to finance hold. I will request metering logs and DB snapshots from SRE. SLA first response satisfied. Assigned to billing + metering teams.

2026-03-10 14:22 - Mateo Alvarez (Metering): Observed 2-minute postback skew from eu-west ingestion queue. Preparing dedupe script; suspect duplicate normalization after rate-map change. Will provide diffs by EOD.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Diego Martinez (Billing): Reproduced a similar negative adjustment on staging when running cache-recon-v2 with 'allow_credit=true' flag. Default should have been 'false' for mid-cycle runs. Continuing to audit job flags and configuration rollout history.

2026-03-12 10:17 - Priya Raman: Collected preliminary diffs. There are ~3.4k request_ids with allocation flip and duplicated processing. Preparing an emergency patch to guard against double-credit creation. Will coordinate manual reversal steps with Finance once patch validated.

2026-03-12 13:05 - OpenFleet (customer): Thank you for the updates. Please advise timeline for reversal and whether our reserved commitment will be affected. We prefer no retroactive clawbacks; we just want invoice corrected for this cycle.
investigation_notes: Metering dedupe script shows duplicate normalization produced +12842.50 worth of credits. Root cause appears to be a race: rate_profile change during a high-ingest window combined with cache-recon-v2 'allow_credit' flag being enabled in the rolled job. Next action: disable allow_credit by default and re-run reconciliation with dedupe by request_id. Finance needs a signed approval for manual invoice reversal.
